\section[sūraj]{\hi{सूरज} (sūraj) — the sun}

\label{lesson:HI-C55-sun}



\begin{quote}
Before the new run of words: what did the last two words of the chapter before mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सूरज}}
\textbf{\hi{सूरज}} (\emph{sūraj}) — \textquotedblleft{}the sun\textquotedblright{}.

From Sanskrit \hi{सूर्य} (\emph{sūrya}), and behind that the Proto-Indo-European word for the sun, which also gives Latin \emph{sōl}, Greek \emph{h\'{\={e}}lios}, and English \emph{sun}.

That makes \hi{सूरज} a cousin of \emph{solar} and of \emph{sun} at once — the Latin word arriving in English through scholarship, the inherited one having been there all along. Same root, two doors.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The first of five things overhead.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūraj}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūraj}, and hear \emph{sol} inside it
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kandhā}, then read \textbf{\hi{गाय}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सूरज} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}the sun\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[chā̃d]{\hi{चाँद} (chā̃d) — the moon}

\label{lesson:HI-C55-moon}



\begin{quote}
What did the word before this one mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चाँद}}
\textbf{\hi{चाँद}} (\emph{chā̃d}) — \textquotedblleft{}the moon\textquotedblright{}.

From Sanskrit \hi{चन्द्र} (\emph{candra}), 'shining, the moon', on a root meaning 'to glow'. The moon is named for what it does, not for what it is.

The same root surfaces in Latin \emph{candēre}, 'to shine white' — which is where English gets \emph{candle}, \emph{candid} and \emph{incandescent}. A candle and the moon are the same idea in two languages.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The second of five, and a word that means 'the shining one'.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chā̃d}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chā̃d}, then \emph{sūraj} — night first, then day
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{ghuṭnā}, then say \emph{ghoṛā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चाँद} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}the moon\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tārā]{\hi{तारा} (tārā) — a star}

\label{lesson:HI-C55-star}



\begin{quote}
Name the 2 words of this chapter so far.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{तारा}}
\textbf{\hi{तारा}} (\emph{tārā}) — \textquotedblleft{}a star\textquotedblright{}.

From Sanskrit \hi{तारा} (\emph{tārā}), 'star', from the reconstructed \emph{h\textsubscript{2}st\'{\={e}}r} — the same root as Latin \emph{stella}, Greek \emph{ast\'{\={e}}r}, and English \emph{star}.

So the three biggest things in the sky are, in Hindi, three separate PIE inheritances: \hi{सूरज} with \emph{sun}, \hi{चाँद} with \emph{candle}, \hi{तारा} with \emph{star}. Three for three, all genuine, which is rarer than it sounds.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The third of five, and the third clean cousin in a row.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tārā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tārā}, and hear \emph{star} in it
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{māthā}, then say \emph{machhlī}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{तारा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}a star\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bādal]{\hi{बादल} (bādal) — a cloud}

\label{lesson:HI-C55-cloud}



\begin{quote}
Name the 3 words of this chapter so far.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बादल}}
\textbf{\hi{बादल}} (\emph{bādal}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cloud\textquotedblright{}.

\hi{बादल} is usually traced to a Sanskrit adjective for 'cloudy' built on \hi{वारि} (\emph{vāri}), 'water', though the route is less tidy than the three words before it and the sources do not all agree on the steps.

That is worth marking. Three clean etymologies in a row can make the fourth look clean too, and this one is not — it is probable rather than settled, and the difference matters.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The fourth of five, and the first this chapter has had to hedge on.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bādal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bādal}, and let the doubt sit there
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\hi{पीठ}}, then say \emph{chiṛiyā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बादल} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}a cloud\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āsmān]{\hi{आसमान} (āsmān) — the sky}

\label{lesson:HI-C55-sky}



\begin{quote}
Name the 4 words of this chapter so far.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{आसमान}}
\textbf{\hi{आसमान}} (\emph{āsmān}) — \textquotedblleft{}the sky\textquotedblright{}.

A Persian word, \emph{āsmān}, whose older Iranian form is a cousin of Sanskrit \hi{अश्मन्} (\emph{aśman}) — and \emph{aśman} means 'stone'. The sky was imagined as a stone vault overhead.

Sanskrit's own everyday word for sky, \hi{आकाश} (\emph{ākāśa}), is a different word from a different root, and Hindi has both. So the sky above a Hindi speaker can be a Persian stone dome or a Sanskrit open space, depending on which word is reached for.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The fifth of five. The sky is furnished.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsmān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsmān}, and under it \emph{sūraj}, \emph{chā̃d}, \emph{tārā}, \emph{bādal}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{hoṇṭh}, then read \textbf{\hi{बकरी}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{आसमान} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}the sky\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
